title: Spring warmth gave no clear change in the northward Orange-tip flight-date delay in England and Wales in 1985-2024
abstract: We tested whether March-April warmth changes the northward delay in Orange-tip mean flight dates. Four site and year effect models used 16,241 site-years in England and Wales in 1985-2004 and 2005-2024. The temperature-by-northing slopes were -0.439 and +0.173 days per 100 km per degree C in England, and +0.378 and +0.117 in Wales. All four adjusted intervals included zero. All count, coverage, survey-boundary and short serial-dependence check intervals also included zero. These results do not establish spatial compression or a fixed spatial gap. Missing visits, survey truncation, changing site coverage, coarse weather and few Welsh sites limit inference. This is an association test, not a causal climate or pollution test. The package provides code, source hashes, aggregate results and a figure. External source data and record-level tables stay outside the signed bundle.

display.caption: Spring temperature interaction with northing in four samples. All adjusted intervals include zero. Negative values indicate a reduced northward flight-date delay in warm years. Contains UKBMS data © Butterfly Conservation, UKCEH, BTO and JNCC. Weather: Met Office.

citations.reason: Related same-archive Orange-tip flight-spread study. We test a spatial interaction, not within-site spread or a period contrast.
